title: Lesson 2 Quiz: Taxation and Redistribution
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin); do not give to students.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A tax takes $1,500 from a household earning $30,000 and $4,000 from a household earning $100,000. How is this tax classified?

choices.text: Progressive, because the richer household pays more dollars
Regressive, because the richer household pays a smaller share
Proportional, because both pay a similar number of dollars
Progressive, because the share paid rises along with income

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: An income tax charges 0% on the first $12,000, 15% on income from $12,000 to $50,000, and 25% on income above $50,000. What is the average tax rate for someone earning $80,000? Round to one decimal place. (Enter a number in percent, without the % sign.)
In a static model with no behavioral response, what does a flat income tax combined with an equal cash payment to every household do to the income distribution?

choices.text: It leaves the distribution unchanged, since the tax rate is the same
It widens the gaps, since richer households pay more dollars in tax
It is regressive overall, since poorer households pay the same rate
It narrows the gaps, since the net tax rate rises as income rises

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Country N has a flat income tax of 25% and pays every household an equal transfer of $6,000 a year. Assuming no behavioral response, at what market income does a household pay exactly as much in tax as it receives in the transfer? (Enter a number in dollars, without the $ sign or commas.)
Which of these is a contested empirical question rather than an arithmetic or definitional fact?

choices.text: How much people cut their work hours when marginal tax rates rise
Whether a higher marginal rate leaves less of each extra dollar earned
Whether a fixed-dollar fee takes a larger share of a smaller income
Whether the average tax rate equals total tax divided by income
